scenes.headline: #2 *GOOGLE FLOW*
scenes.say: Number two, Google Flow: fifty free credits a day, enough for about five short Veo Lite clips at current rates.
That's straight from Google's help page, and at peak hours, free users might not get any videos at all.

scenes.say: And number one is Wan 2.2: open-source video generation, with its smaller model targeting a {24|twenty-four} gigabyte GPU.

cons: Flow: daily credits expire; no free 1080p upscale
Dreamina: export rules depend on plan/settings
scenes.say: The catch? Flow's daily credits don't roll over, and free accounts can't upscale to {1080p|ten-eighty p}. Wan has no service credit cap, but hardware isn't free.
So which one are you trying first? Comment {FREE|free}.

verify_before_render: DONE 2026-10-09: support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234: 'With or without a subscription, you receive 50 Google Flow credits per day'; unused daily credits don't roll over; Veo 3.1 Lite = 10 credits per generation for non-Ultra users (4/6/8 s); 1080p upscaling not available to non-subscribers; 'During peak hours, roughly 2 PM to 5 PM UTC, you may not be able to generate videos without a subscription.'

DONE 2026-10-09: dreamina.capcut.com/tools/seedance-2-0 (ByteDance, official): 'You can try Dreamina Seedance 2.0 using free daily credits'; every paid plan lists 'Remove the Dreamina watermark in downloads' (free downloads are watermarked). Daily amount not published on the page.
DONE 2026-10-09: github.com/Wan-Video/Wan2.2: Apache-2.0 (GitHub API), 17,806 stars; README: TI2V-5B 720P at 24 FPS, 'can run on a GPU with at least 24GB VRAM (e.g, RTX 4090 GPU)'.

DONE 2026-10-09: footage = official samples: Google DeepMind Veo page covers (storage.googleapis.com), Dreamina Seedance 2.0 page videos (capcutcdn), Wan2.2 README demo. Avoided Dreamina samples with third-party IP (Stranger Things, Encanto-like).

2026-10-10: official Google Flow help reconfirmed 50 daily credits, Veo 3.1 Lite 10 credits for non-Ultra users, peak-hour restrictions and no free upscaling. Official Dreamina pricing/guide says watermark policies vary; narration corrected before publication. Wan2.2 README: TI2V-5B single-GPU command >=24 GB VRAM.

youtube.description:
3 AI video generators you can try without a subscription, with the actual trade-offs. Dreamina Seedance 2.0 gives free daily credits; watermark/export rules vary by plan, model and settings. Google Flow gives 50 credits/day; Veo 3.1 Lite costs 10 per generation, so about five clips if access is available. Free generation may be unavailable at peak hours, credits do not roll over, and free accounts cannot upscale to 1080p. Wan2.2 has no hosted-service credit cap when self-hosted, but its 5B model targets a 24 GB GPU and hardware/electricity are not free.
Checked October 10, 2026; limits can change.
Sources: support.google.com/flow, dreamina.capcut.com, github.com/Wan-Video/Wan2.2. AI-generated demo footage from the official makers.
